npcs.name: Wren Piper
npcs.idle: Pip's always off somewhere. Usually he comes back.

npcs.name: Old Corwen
npcs.idle: The river gives, the river takes. Mostly it takes, this year.

npcs.name: Sister Aldith
npcs.idle: Pray for the filidh, if you pray. Somebody must.

npcs.name: Hedda the Woodcutter
npcs.idle: Wood doesn't cut itself. More's the pity.

npcs.name: Reeve Gwenda
npcs.idle: Ludlow sent forty men to Camlann. Eleven came home. The other twenty-nine are in the graveyard, and they won't stay there.

npcs.name: Huw the Ferryman
npcs.idle: I've ferried the living across this river thirty years. Lately the dead want a ride.

npcs.name: Sergeant Mabyn
npcs.idle: Humberton keep. Four walls, one gate and nowhere near enough men.

npcs.name: Prior Anselm
npcs.idle: Vetusta's bell has rung the hours for three hundred years. It hasn't rung since the Bishop's new brothers came.

npcs.name: Brother Teilo
npcs.idle: They threw us out with nothing but our habits. I kept my psalter. I'll have the abbey back too.

npcs.name: Scout Morfudd
npcs.idle: Goblins I can count. What the goblins are carrying out of that mine, I don't like.

quests.title: The Singing Bridge
quests.offer:
Have you seen my brother? He's this tall, and loud, and he's called Pip. He went to the [singing bridge] last night and he's not back.

Our Da drowned crossing there in the winter. Pip says he can hear Da singing from the water at night. He's ten. Will you [find Pip]? Old Corwen knows the bridge.

topics.singing bridge: The magic bridge, up the river to the north. People say it sings. Pip says it sings with Da's voice.

quests.summary: Wren Piper's little brother Pip went to the singing bridge where their father drowned.

steps.goal: Ask Old Corwen about the singing bridge
steps.say: The magic bridge, up the river? Aye, it sings. Or the goblins do, on the north end, when they're fishing. Singing at night with voices they've no right to. I've heard my own mother calling from that water, and she's thirty years buried. Pip went up to the [north end], I'd guess.

steps.goal: Search the north end of the magic bridge
steps.text: Pip's satchel. Inside: a heel of bread, a wooden whistle, and a drawing of goblins, with an arrow pointing west and 'DA?' in big letters.

steps.goal: Deal with the goblin fishermen west of the bridge
steps.text: One of the goblins drops a reed whistle. When you blow it, it doesn't sound like a whistle. It sounds like a man calling a boy's name. They took Pip to their singer.

steps.goal: Find Pip at the goblins' singing-pool
steps.text: The singer's whistles scatter. In the reeds, a very muddy boy is hiding.

stages.name: Gobble-Eye the Singer
stages.announce: A goblin with a necklace of whistles stands up out of the pool and sings - in a drowned man's voice. 'Pip! Come here, Pip!'

steps.goal: Talk to Pip
steps.say:
It wasn't Da. Was it. It was him. With the whistles.

I knew, really. I just wanted to hear it again. Don't tell Wren I cried. Let's go [home].

steps.goal: Bring Pip home to Wren
steps.say:
PIP! You horrible - come here. Come HERE.

...What was it? What did he hear? You can tell me [the truth]. Or you can say it was [only the river]. I think I know which he needs. I'm not sure which I do.

options.say:
A goblin. Using Da's voice. Gods.

I'm glad you said. I'd rather hate a goblin than wonder for the rest of my life. Thank you.

The river. Yes. The river does that.

Pip's asleep already. He said Da sang him a song before the goblins came. I'm going to let him keep it.

truth.text: Pip wants you to have this - it was Da's.

river.text: Pip wants you to have this - it was Da's.

quests.title: One Willing Heart
quests.offer:
Brother Osric is young and kind and thinks that's armour. He went north to preach to the filidh at their standing stone - to turn them from blood. His letters came every week.

They stopped a fortnight ago. Hedda the woodcutter works up that way. Will you [go north] and see what's become of him?
quests.summary: Brother Osric went north to preach to the filidh at their standing stone, and his letters stopped coming.

steps.goal: Ask Hedda the woodcutter about the friar
steps.say: The young monk? Saw him a week back, walking with the filidh. Not tied - walking, smiling, talking with them like old friends. Gave me a blessing on his way past. Odd thing is, they were all smiling. Up at the [stones].

steps.goal: Search the path to the northern standing stone

clue.name: a dropped satchel and a torn page

steps.text: An unfinished letter, in a careful hand: 'Sister - they are kind to me. They say the stone does not want blood, only one willing heart, once in a generation. I think I understand them now. I think I am glad.'

steps.goal: Fight through the devout filidh at the stone
steps.text: Garlands of white flowers hang on the menhir. Someone has laid out a friar's habit, folded, on the altar-stone.

steps.goal: Reach Osric before the rite ends
steps.text: The rite is broken. The menhir is only a stone again.

stages.name: Keep Brother Osric alive
stages.announce: Osric stands by the stone, garlanded, eyes shut. The filidh begin to chant, and the sickles come out.
stages.thanks: I... I was going to let them. I was GLAD.

stages.name: Archfilidh Corra
stages.announce: A tall woman in white steps out from behind the stone. 'He came to us willing. You have no right.'

steps.goal: Talk to Brother Osric
steps.say:
I came to save them and they nearly saved me - that's what it felt like. Being wanted that much.

I don't know what I am now. Sister Aldith will want me [home]. But the filidh who are left - they're frightened now, and lost. Someone kind should [stay] with them. Tell me what to do. I can't trust myself to choose.

options.say: Home. Yes. I'll walk behind you. Tell her... tell her I'm sorry about the letters.
Then I'll stay. Not as a sacrifice - as a friar. Take her my letter. All of it. She should know what I nearly did.

steps.goal: Return to Sister Aldith
steps.say:
He came in, and knelt, and wouldn't get up until I made him. He's sleeping now, in his old cell.

I have read his last letter. I will burn it, I think. He doesn't need to remember being glad.

steps.goal: Return to Sister Aldith
steps.say:
He stayed. With them. After that.

He was always braver than me, and stupider. I will pray for him every day, and I will write every week, and if one week he doesn't answer, I am going up there myself.

home.text: Take this, for bringing him back to us.

stayed.text: Take this. He'd want you to have something of his.

quests.title: Ants in the Cabbages
quests.offer:
Ants. The size of cats, in my cabbages. They come up from a hill south of the road and strip a field in a night.

I can't spare the Watch for ants. Will you [stop the ants]? Break up their hill and they'll go somewhere else.
quests.summary: Giant ants from a hill south of Ludlow are stripping the fields.

steps.goal: Kill the ants in Ludlow's fields about 130 m north of Reeve Gwenda
Break up the anthill south of the road
Tell Reeve Gwenda
steps.say: Cabbages. Saved. You'd laugh, but that's half of Ludlow's winter.

quests.title: The Men Who Came Home
quests.offer:
Ludlow sent forty men to Camlann with the King. Twenty-nine came home in carts, and we buried them in the graveyard north of the road.

This month they've started getting up. Bones walking among the stones, and hounds that aren't there howling in the fields. Will you [go to the graveyard]? Find out who's waking them.
quests.summary: The Camlann dead of Ludlow are rising from their graves.

steps.goal: Lay the risen dead in Ludlow graveyard to rest about 240 m north-west of Reeve Gwenda
Kill the spectral hounds in the fields
Search the graves that were opened

clue.name: an opened grave with a red cord on the stone

steps.text: Every opened grave has a red cord knotted round its headstone, thirteen knots each. Someone came at night, and tied them, and went away.

steps.goal: Show the red cord to Reeve Gwenda
steps.say:
Thirteen knots. The new brothers up at Vetusta wear cords like this round their waists. Red ones.

Prior Anselm is in Humberton - they threw him out of his own abbey. He'll know what it means.

default.text: From Reeve Gwenda, for Ludlow's dead.

quests.title: The Drowned Reach
quests.offer:
The goblins fish this river. Fished, I should say - the drowned ones are getting up out of it now, still holding their nets. Grey and wet and walking.

The river doesn't do that by itself. Will you [search the reach]? Upstream, where the water's slow and deep.
quests.summary: Drowned goblin fishermen are rising from the river. Huw the Ferryman wants to know why.

steps.goal: Put down the drowned fishermen in the reach about 150 m north of Huw the Ferryman
Search the riverbed in the slow water

clue.name: a black stone on the riverbed

steps.text: A black stone sunk in the mud, a red key on it, and round it a ring of bones - not goblin bones. Old, big, and wrapped in rotted mail.

steps.goal: Kill the drowned warriors at the singing pool
Tell Huw what you found
steps.say:
Men's bones in mail, at the bottom of my river? There's no battlefield on this river.

...Unless someone carried them here. From somewhere else.

quests.title: The Mother of the Marsh
quests.offer:
There's a marsh south of Ludlow, and something in it laying eggs. The slith broodlings come up into the road at dusk now.

The mother's called Slith - the old women named her. Will you [go to the marsh]?
quests.summary: Slith broodlings from the marsh south of Ludlow are coming up into the road.

steps.goal: Kill the slith broodlings in the marsh about 310 m south of Reeve Gwenda
Kill Slith, the mother of the marsh
steps.text: Slith thrashes once in the reeds, and lies still.

steps.goal: Tell Reeve Gwenda
steps.say: The old women'll be disappointed. They liked having a monster.

quests.title: Robbers' Landing
quests.offer:
Robbers have taken the old landing west of my ferry. They wait for the boats and take everything - and the strange thing is, they let some folk by.

Will you [clear the landing]? And find out who they let pass.
quests.summary: Robbers have taken the old landing on the river west of the ferry.

steps.goal: Clear the robbers from the landing about 190 m west of Huw the Ferryman
Search the robbers' lean-to

clue.name: a lean-to of oars and sailcloth

steps.text: A note, scrawled: 'Them as wears the red cord, let by. The Bishop pays.'

steps.goal: Tell Huw
steps.say: 'The Bishop pays.' Robbers, paid by a bishop. I've lived too long.

quests.title: The Ludlow Highway
quests.offer:
My couriers to Ludlow aren't arriving. The road north-east of the town goes through a cut, and there's a gang of highwaymen in it.

The last courier was carrying my report on the abbey. Will you [find my courier]? Or what's left of him.
quests.summary: Watch couriers on the Ludlow road are being ambushed by highwaymen.

steps.goal: Clear the bandits on the highway about 610 m east of Sergeant Mabyn
Kill the highwaymen in the cut
Search the ambush for the courier's satchel
steps.text: The courier's report is gone. In its place, a red cord with thirteen knots - left on purpose.

steps.goal: Tell Sergeant Mabyn
steps.say:
They took my report on the abbey and left me a calling card. The Bishop wants me to know he knows.

Well. Now I know too.

quests.title: Webs over the North Road
quests.offer:
A messenger from the northern outpost left four days ago and never arrived. The forest north of the river is full of giant spiders.

Will you [search the forest]? Spiders keep what they catch. He might still be alive.
quests.summary: A Watch messenger went missing in the spider-ridden forest north of the river.

steps.goal: Kill the giant spiders in the north forest about 720 m north of Sergeant Mabyn
Search the webs for the messenger
steps.text: You cut the cocoon open. Inside, the messenger - grey, half-starved and very much alive. 'Water,' he croaks. 'And tell the sergeant... goblins. Carrying bones south.'

steps.goal: Tell Sergeant Mabyn
steps.say: Alive! God be thanked. Bones south... from the mine? Scout Morfudd's at the northern outpost. She'll want to hear it.

quests.title: The Nain Raids
quests.offer:
Dwarves. Nain, they call themselves - not like the pilgrims in Camelot Hills; these came down out of the west hills this spring and they've been raiding Humberton's farms ever since.

Their war-leader is called Frund. Will you [stop the raids]?
quests.summary: Nain dwarves from the west hills are raiding Humberton's farms.

steps.goal: Fight off the nain raiders on the west road about 330 m south-west of Sergeant Mabyn
Defeat Frund, the nain war-leader
steps.text: Frund falls. 'Red-hand men burned our halls,' he gasps. 'We only took back what we lost.'

steps.goal: Tell Sergeant Mabyn what Frund said
steps.say:
Red-hand men burned their halls? The Crimson, again - driving the nain onto us, to keep my men busy. The same trick they played in Camelot Hills.

We could [make peace] with the nain - send them grain and an apology. Or [hold the line]; raiders are raiders.

options.say: Grain and an apology. And maybe one day an axe on our side when the Crimson come.
Then the west road stays guarded. Thank you for Frund, at least.

peace.text: The nain send a gift down from the hills.

quests.title: Red Dwarves of the East Wood
quests.offer:
Red dwarves in the east woods - thieves, every one. They take tools, pots, anything metal. Now they've taken the church bell's clapper, and Ludlow can't ring for its dead.

Their camp's in the far north-east, and their chief is Agisthil. Will you [get the clapper back]?
quests.summary: Red dwarf thieves from the east woods stole Ludlow church's bell clapper.

steps.goal: Fight through the red dwarf thieves in the east woods about 530 m north of Reeve Gwenda
Defeat Agisthil at the red dwarf camp
Search the camp for the clapper
steps.text: Pots, nails, horseshoes - and the iron clapper of Ludlow's bell, wrapped in a red cord. Somebody paid them to take it.

steps.goal: Return the clapper to Reeve Gwenda
steps.say:
Our bell! Now Ludlow can ring for its dead again - and lay them down properly.

Somebody doesn't want bells rung in these mountains. I wonder why.

quests.title: Bones Going South
quests.offer:
The goblins of Tepok's Mine have been coming out at night with sacks. Heavy sacks. They carry them south to the river and come back with silver.

Will you [stop a sack]? Kill their scouts on the raid path and see what they're carrying.

topics.mount badon: Arthur's great victory, twelve battles in. The Saxons broke and there was peace for a generation.

quests.summary: The goblins of Tepok's Mine carry heavy sacks south to the river by night.

steps.goal: Kill the goblin scouts on the raid path about 320 m south-west of Scout Morfudd
Open a goblin's sack

clue.name: a heavy sack, dropped in the bracken

steps.text: Bones. A man's - big, old, and with a rusted torc round the neck. A brooch in the sack: a red dragon on a field of gold.

steps.goal: Show the brooch to Scout Morfudd
steps.say:
The red dragon. That's Arthur's. That's the badge his men wore at Mount Badon, before any of us were born.

The goblins have dug into a cairn of Arthur's dead.

quests.title: What the Goblins Dug
quests.offer:
The goblins broke into the cairn and found it full - Arthur's men from Badon, buried with their arms. Somebody's buying the bones. And the drowned in the river, Huw says, wear old mail.

Grilk leads the diggers. Will you [close the cairn]? Kill Grilk and see what's left in the mine mouth.
quests.summary: The goblins of Tepok's Mine have broken into a cairn of Arthur's dead from Mount Badon and sell the bones.

steps.goal: Fight into the goblin camp about 330 m west of Scout Morfudd
Defeat Grilk, who leads the diggers
Search the mine mouth

clue.name: a cart of bones, and a ledger

steps.text: A cart of bones, sorted and labelled, and a goblin ledger in a very human hand: 'Bones of Badon, by the cart, to the river. For the Bishop: these remember how to fight.'

steps.goal: Tell Scout Morfudd what you found
steps.say:
'These remember how to fight.' He's raising an army from Arthur's own dead. God.

We can [rebury them] in the cairn, and seal it. Or [carry them to Ludlow] and lay them in holy ground beside the Camlann men.

options.say: Back to the cairn, and stones over the door. They'll rest where they fell.
Ludlow's bell will ring for them. Gwenda will see to it.

ludlow.text: Ludlow rings its bell for Badon's dead.

quests.title: The Great Gobzini
quests.offer:
One goblin knows the price of bones better than the rest: the Great Gobzini, a conjurer, who sits in the far north corner of the hills and does the Bishop's bargaining. The Goblin Lord does what he says.

Will you [end the trade]? You'll want friends - he's no fool.
quests.summary: The Great Gobzini, a goblin conjurer, bargains the bones of Badon to the Bishop.

steps.goal: Defeat the Goblin Lord about 430 m west of Scout Morfudd
Defeat the Great Gobzini
steps.text: Gobzini goes up in a puff of green smoke and doesn't come down.

steps.goal: Tell Scout Morfudd
steps.say: No Gobzini, no bargain. The trade's done. Now it's only the Bishop.

quests.title: The Summoner in the West Field
quests.offer:
There's a man in the field west of Humberton who calls things up out of the ground. Salizern, he calls himself. He came the week the new brothers came to Vetusta.

Will you [deal with him]? Bring me whatever he carries.
quests.summary: A summoner called Salizern calls things up in the field west of Humberton.

steps.goal: Defeat Summoner Salizern about 210 m west of Sergeant Mabyn
Tell Sergeant Mabyn
steps.say: He carried a red cord too? Of course he did. Every rat in these mountains wears one.

quests.title: The Bishop's Letters
quests.offer:
Bishop Burhoff came to us two years ago, a good man, we thought. Then this spring he brought in new brothers who wore red cords. In a month they had the abbey, and we had the road.

If the Bishop is in league with someone, it'll be in his letters - he keeps a writing-desk in the cloister. Will you [find the letters]?
quests.summary: Prior Anselm, driven out of Vetusta Abbey, thinks Bishop Burhoff's letters will show who he serves.

steps.goal: Fight through the dark brothers in the cloister about 350 m south of Prior Anselm
Search the Bishop's writing-desk
steps.text: Letters, in the fine crowned hand you know from Mithra's Tomb: 'Burhoff - Malgwyn is lost. Gather what Badon gives you. When the stones of Salisbury wake, march. M.'

steps.goal: Bring the letters to Prior Anselm
steps.say:
M. Morgana. In our abbey. Under our bell.

'When the stones of Salisbury wake'... I don't know what that means, and I don't want to. We must take Vetusta back before it does.

quests.title: The Bells of Vetusta
quests.offer:
The Prior says the bell won't ring because they've bound it. If the bell rings, every true brother hiding in these hills will know the abbey's ours again - and the Bishop's men will know too.

I'll ring it. Will you [guard the tower] while I do? It'll take a while to cut the cords.
quests.summary: Brother Teilo means to ring Vetusta's bound bell and call the true brothers home.

steps.goal: Clear the dark brothers-in-arms from the abbey yard about 430 m south of Brother Teilo
Keep Brother Teilo alive while he cuts the bell free
steps.text: The bell swings, and rings - once, twice, and then a long peal across the mountains.

stages.name: Keep Brother Teilo alive
stages.announce: Teilo throws off his cloak and starts sawing at the red cords. 'Hold the stair! They're coming!'

steps.goal: Tell Prior Anselm
steps.say:
I heard it. All of Humberton heard it. Brothers are coming down out of the hills already.

The Bishop heard it too.

quests.title: The Dark Bishop
quests.offer:
The bell's rung and the brothers are home - but Burhoff still holds the crypt below the abbey's south wall, with his best.

This ends it. Will you [face the Bishop]? Bring as many friends as will come.
quests.summary: Dark Bishop Burhoff still holds the crypt below Vetusta Abbey.

steps.goal: Go down to the crypt below the abbey's south wall about 480 m south of Prior Anselm
steps.text: The crypt stairs are wet, and you can hear chanting below.

steps.goal: Defeat Dark Bishop Burhoff
steps.text: Burhoff falls against the altar. 'She'll come,' he says. 'Through the gate in the lake. And the giants will dance for her on Salisbury Plain.'

steps.goal: Search the Bishop's altar

clue.name: an altar with a red key

steps.text: A map of Salisbury Plain, with a ring of stones drawn on it in red. And written beside it: 'The Giants' Dance. Merlin built it. Merlin's stones will open for me.'

steps.goal: Bring the map to Prior Anselm
steps.say:
The Giants' Dance - the stones at Salisbury, that Merlin raised over the dead of Britain. She means to use them.

Vetusta is ours again, and you gave it back to us. Carry this map to the Watch on Salisbury Plain. And come home when you can; the bell will ring for you.

default.text: From the Abbey Faithful, with the bell's blessing.
